idiom_name: Component => Component function composition; curried enhancer factories
implementation_notes: Functions are first-class values in Scala - the official tour states that higher-order functions take functions as parameters or return a function - so an enhancer is literally a value of type Component => Component and composing enhancers is function composition, with no wrapper class required. Currying (def withAuth(config)(component: Component)) turns a configured enhancer into a single-argument one that composes cleanly, and in Scala.js UI layers the component is a Modifier/Html value that an enhancer takes and returns, with given/implicit context supplying cross-cutting values. A named wrapper class is still justified when the framework needs a stable component type (ScalaFX/Swing nodes) or when the enhancement participates in a lifecycle.
pitfalls: Implicit/given resolution is lexical: a value required by the enhancer can be picked up from a different scope than the application site, so cross-cutting values should be passed explicitly where the call site matters.

By-name and function parameters change evaluation semantics: an enhancer that takes the component by name can re-evaluate it on every call, breaking referential transparency and causing repeated rendering.
Scala.js interop with JavaScript components bypasses the type system: a foreign component typed as Component still needs a runtime shape check before it is wrapped.
